INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About Visual Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module lets you inspect the invariant-mass results collected by students in a selected session.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose a session from the dropdown above the Results table.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The Mass Histograms show the combined distribution of particle masses reported by the selected students.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: In the Results table, select or deselect students to include or exclude their data from the histograms.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_4: Use the refresh button if new student results become available.
INSTRUCTIONS.HOW_TO_READ_INTRO: Each histogram shows the invariant mass of a candidate particle:
INSTRUCTIONS.CLEAR_PEAK: A clear peak indicates that students correctly identified that particle.
INSTRUCTIONS.BROAD_DISTRIBUTION: A broad or flat distribution may mean misidentification or too few candidates.
INSTRUCTIONS.TIP: Compare histograms across students or sessions to see how consistently the class reconstructed each particle species.

INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About Large Scale Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module combines results from a masterclass event to study strangeness enhancement - how the production of strange particles increases in heavy-ion Pb-Pb collisions relative to proton-proton collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose an event from the dropdown above the plot.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The plot shows strangeness enhancement as a function of collision centrality, measured by No. participants.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: The Results table lists yields and enhancement values for each centrality class and particle species.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_4: Use the refresh button if new results become available.
INSTRUCTIONS.YIELD_DEF: efficiency-corrected yield per event: reconstructed particle count divided by (number of analysed events × reconstruction efficiency)
INSTRUCTIONS.NPART_DEF: average number of nucleons participating in the collision
INSTRUCTIONS.NO_PARTICLE_DEF: average student signal from the Large Scale Analysis fit for that centrality class and particle species: excess of counts over the combinatorial background under the peak
INSTRUCTIONS.ENHANCEMENT_DEF: yield per participant, normalised to a pp reference:
INSTRUCTIONS.WHERE_YPP: where Ypp is the reference yield in pp collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.FACTOR_TWO: The factor 2 converts the pp yield to a per-participant scale, since a pp collision involves two protons.
INSTRUCTIONS.LOOK_FOR: Enhancement is usually larger for more central collisions with higher No. participants and can differ between
INSTRUCTIONS.LOOK_FOR_END: Discuss with students why denser collisions may produce more strange quarks.
INSTRUCTIONS.TIP: Use the coloured markers in the table together with the plot to connect a specific centrality class to its point on the graph.

INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About R_AA Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module turns the J/psi yield students measure in Pb-Pb collisions into the nuclear modification factor RAA - a measure of how J/psi production in Pb-Pb collisions is suppressed or enhanced relative to a simple superposition of independent proton-proton collisions. Students can still analyse and submit pp and p-Pb signals as part of the exercise, but only the Pb-Pb centrality classes appear in the table below.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose an event from the dropdown above the plot.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The plot shows R_AA as a function of collision centrality, measured by No. participants, for the eight Pb-Pb centrality classes.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: The Results table lists only the eight Pb-Pb centrality classes, each with its raw signal, Acc × ε, corrected yield and R_AA. A student's own pp/p-Pb signal is still accepted by the exercise but is not shown here.
INSTRUCTIONS.NO_JPSI_DEF: the fitted J/psi signal from the residual-fit yield extraction (unlike-sign minus like-sign pairs), with its Poisson error
INSTRUCTIONS.EFFICIENCY_DEF: the full acceptance × efficiency (A × ε, including PID) for that collision system - centrality-dependent for Pb-Pb, flat for pp and p-Pb. Calibrated to the same fixed-width mass window the student app locks the signal slider to.
INSTRUCTIONS.YIELD_DEF: the Acc × ε- and branching-ratio-corrected inclusive yield per event:
INSTRUCTIONS.NCOLL_DEF: average number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions in that centrality class (Glauber Monte Carlo)
INSTRUCTIONS.RAA_DEF: the Pb-Pb yield divided by what Ncoll independent pp collisions would have produced, using a fixed physical pp reference yield at 5.02 TeV (not the student's own measurement - see below):
INSTRUCTIONS.PP_REFERENCE_NOTE: R_AA compares two different collision systems - it does not require them to be measured at the same collision energy, and even theoretical R_AA predictions routinely compare Pb-Pb at 5.02 TeV against pp at other energies. The real reason a student's own pp/p-Pb measurement cannot be the R<sub>AA</sub> denominator is that the pp/p-Pb exercise sample is deliberately enriched in J/ψ, so that fitting a visible peak is possible in the time available - the same simplification already used for the enhancement calculation in the Strangeness Large Scale Analysis module. Using the enriched sample directly would make R<sub>AA</sub> come out several orders of magnitude too low. R<sub>AA</sub> therefore uses a fixed reference yield computed from the published inclusive J/ψ cross section and inelastic cross section at 5.02 TeV - the same approach the Large Scale Analysis module uses for its own fixed pp reference yields. Students can still analyse and submit their own pp/p-Pb signal as part of the exercise, but it is not shown in this table and never enters R<sub>AA</sub>.
INSTRUCTIONS.WINDOW_NOTE: The A × ε constants are calibrated to a specific mass window (2.92–3.16 GeV/c², width 0.24 GeV/c²). The student app locks the signal-counting window to that same width (0.25 GeV/c² for pp/p-Pb, 0.24 GeV/c² for Pb-Pb); students can only slide it, not resize it. Because the width always matches the calibration, no extra mass-window correction is applied to A × ε.
INSTRUCTIONS.LOOK_FOR: R_AA below 1 indicates suppression of J/psi production in Pb-Pb collisions (e.g. from colour screening in the quark-gluon plasma); R_AA above 1 would indicate enhancement. pp and p-Pb are not shown in this table - they are not part of the R_AA calculation.
INSTRUCTIONS.TIP: The dashed line on the plot marks R_AA = 1, i.e. no nuclear modification.

INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About Event Exploration
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module collects the part-1 nuclear modification factors the students measured by counting charged primary tracks in 30 pp events and in the three Pb–Pb events (peripheral, semi-central, central).
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose a session from the dropdown above the Results table.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: In the Results table, select or deselect students to include or exclude their measurements from the plots.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: Each row shows the two numbers a student reports per class: RAA over all pT, and RAA restricted to pT > 1 GeV/c.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_4: Use the refresh button when more students have uploaded their results.
INSTRUCTIONS.HOW_TO_READ_INTRO: The six pads follow the layout of the desktop instructor tool: rows are the three Pb–Pb centrality classes, columns are the two p<sub>T</sub> windows.
INSTRUCTIONS.READ_COLUMNS: Left column: RAA from all charged primaries. Right column: only tracks with pT > 1 GeV/c, drawn with open markers.
INSTRUCTIONS.READ_UNITY: The grey dashed line marks R<sub>AA</sub> = 1, the value expected if a Pb–Pb collision were just a superposition of independent nucleon–nucleon collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.READ_MEAN: The coloured dashed line is the mean over the selected students; the header shows that mean and how many students it averages.
INSTRUCTIONS.READ_SPREAD: The scatter around the mean is the statistical spread of a single-event measurement — expect it to be large, and larger for peripheral than for central collisions.
